To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
common variants in FTO are associated with increased obesity in women with current BMI > 35 kg/m 2 and lifetime BMI > 40 kg/m 2.
common genetic variation at the FTO gene is associated with increased risk of obesity.
we found that the FTO gene is associated with obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of obesity and its genetic basis.
the identification of genes that are involved in the regulation of body weight and body composition.
the genetic factors that contribute to the risk of obesity and its comorbidities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the association of obesity with common genetic variation in FTO is robust and replicates in a large number of independent studies.
the FTO gene has been found to be associated with obesity and obesity related traits in several studies, but the mechanism by which it exerts its effect remains to be determined.
FTO is associated, in the population studied, with increased risk of obesity, and this association is consistent with a major gene effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FTO variants are strongly associated with extreme obesity, and that these variants may account for differences in obesity risk between closely related individuals.
common variation in FTO may in part account, at least in some individuals, for differences between closely-related individuals in their risk of obesity.
common genetic variants of FTO influence the risk of obesity in a dose-dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
common variation in FTO is a strong risk factor for obesity.
the FTO gene is associated with obesity in extremely obese women and in extremely discordant pairs of sisters.
common genetic variants can have a major impact on the risk of obesity.
